# Vision Driven Design (VDD)

> Open-source (MIT) spec-driven development methodology and MCP server for AI coding agents. VDD turns a human vision statement into a fully traced delivery chain across 8 phases and three coverage invariants, with bi-directional Vision → Strategy → Tactics → Specs → Plan → Tasks (V→S→A→SP→PL→TK) traceability. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, VS Code and other MCP clients.

## Connect

- Hosted MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, no API key): https://vdd.simonmak.com/api/mcp
- Local stdio server: `npx -y @simonmak-ascent/mcp`
- Hosted mode is stateless: no session, no filesystem. Every tool takes the artifact text as an argument and returns a verdict, so one call is enough.
- Official MCP Registry name: `com.ascent-partners/vision-driven-design`
- Glama listing: https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/simonmak-ascent/vision-driven-design
- Context7 library ID: `/simonmak-ascent/vision-driven-design`

## MCP tools (3) and skills (9)

- `vdd_check`: judge one artifact — invariants A, B, C and the declared counts.
- `vdd_chain_validate`: judge the whole chain, plus every goal reaching a task.
- `vdd_amend`: judge an amendment and list the downstream artifacts it invalidates.

No prompts are shipped: `prompts/list` returns `{prompts: []}`. The nine procedures are served
as `skill://<name>/SKILL.md` (`vdd-constitution`, `vdd-vision`, `vdd-strategy`, `vdd-tactics`,
`vdd-specs`, `vdd-plan`, `vdd-tasks`, `vdd-implement`, `vdd-validate`) through `skills/list`
and `skills/get`.
